source.title: Measuring the Effects of Data Parallelism on Neural Network Training
source.authors: Christopher J. Shallue; Jaehoon Lee; J. Antognini; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein; Roy Frostig; G. Dahl

record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and compares out-of-sample error under step and epoch compute budgets, directly testing the batch-size effect described in V5.
record.gate_note: The study also compares architectures and model sizes for steps to a validation-error goal, but those results do not measure the generalization-gap behavior in the corresponding versions. Label smoothing results are included because they test a regularization change relevant to V5. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch and step budgets, testing V5. Section 4.3 also explicitly reports better attainable MNIST performance for the convolutional model than the fully connected model, bearing on V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find no evidence of an inherent degradation from increasing batch size when tuning and budgets are considered. They explicitly find that fixed epoch budgets favor smaller batches, fixed step budgets favor larger batches, and label smoothing can improve large-batch performance. Near-saturated MNIST differences may be noise; LM1B performance was not saturated.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares batch sizes with independently tuned SGD-family optimizer parameters and reports out-of-sample error under different compute budgets; it does not test arbitrary-label memorization or the full set of conditions named in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported batch-size effect depends on compute-budget type (training steps versus epochs). Label smoothing improves validation error at large batch sizes but has no apparent effect at small batch sizes; it does not change steps to goal when multiple settings achieve the goal.

fits_no_version.finding: Label smoothing does not change steps to the validation target when multiple smoothing settings achieve that target within budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label smoothing can improve attainable validation performance without changing training speed to an already achievable target.

record.problems: The authors report practical limits in tuning: search spaces were specified by hand, optimal metaparameters may not have been found, and maximum or minimum results across trials may not be robust. MNIST and Fashion MNIST batch-size differences were very small and could be due to noise. The language-model workloads did not reach saturated performance within practical training time.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results were included. Section 4.3 and Figures 3–6 compare model architecture, width, depth, and datasets for steps to a validation goal, rather than the generalization-gap measures required by V2 or V3. Cited prior-work outcomes were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization together with natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
The contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, convolution-derived initialization, and comparisons beyond the reported MNIST architecture comparison.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning-dependent held-out differences, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.

Whether warmup or changing normalization removes the penalty across batch sizes under equal epoch budgets. Ghost batch normalization is used without a corresponding normalization ablation; schedule comparisons at one batch size do not establish a warmup rescue.
Dropout ablations, small-training-set exceptions, excessive-dropout underfitting, and jointly removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

missing.what: The authors' own statement that Simple CNN ultimately achieves better MNIST performance than the fully connected model. Record this separately from the steps-to-target comparison; endpoint errors are not given numerically.

Separate test-set error results for Simple CNN on MNIST and Fashion MNIST under step and epoch budgets. Existing rows record validation error only; test curves provide a distinct held-out check, although numerical curve values cannot be read from the supplied text.

Label smoothing generally helps all batch sizes on MNIST and Fashion MNIST, without consistently helping larger batches more. This qualifies the batch-specific regularization benefit reported for ImageNet.

Increasing the L2 penalty and adding Gaussian gradient noise unsuccessfully controlled large-batch overfitting, whereas label smoothing succeeded. These failed adaptations are absent from the recorded rows.

record.verdict_notes: No V5 verdict labels are assigned because arXiv:1811.03600 is an original source for V5. That exclusion does not apply to its incidental V3 result. Language-model cross entropy is a valid held-out performance measure for V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Test-error comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
Held-out performance comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD.
Language-model results use validation cross entropy; the study does not report all adaptation conditions named in the version, such as learning-rate warmup.
Dropout comparisons and removal of dropout and weight decay together.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: Simple CNN on MNIST
rows.size_stated: Base model: 2 convolutional layers and 1 fully connected hidden layer; convolutional layers have 32 and 64 filters, fully connected layer has 1,024 units.
rows.operation_detail: Compared best validation error across batch sizes under step budgets.

conditions.value: training steps; a range of budgets shown in Figure 11a
MNIST

rows.note: The authors state that step budgets favor large batch sizes overall, but do not describe the direction for this individual model and budget condition.
rows.check: Section 4.8 explicitly states that larger batches achieve better held-out error under fixed step budgets. This bears on V5's longer-training qualification because larger batches process more epochs at equal steps; it does not test the fixed-epoch penalty. Exact curve values remain unavailable.

MNIST

rows.note: The authors state that epoch budgets favor small batches overall, but say maximum-performance differences between batch sizes on MNIST are very small or nonexistent.
rows.check: The row combines different budget regimes. Smaller batches perform better under constrained epoch budgets, but near-saturated maximum-performance differences are very small or nonexistent and potentially noise. Split these conditions; do not interpret the saturation result as absence of a penalty at every epoch budget.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Added label smoothing during training and compared validation error across batch sizes.

conditions.value: large; greater than 2^14 without label smoothing could not achieve the goal validation error within the training budget
label smoothing; fixed compute budget per batch size

rows.baseline: as much as one percentage point worse at large batch sizes without label smoothing
rows.value: improved by as much as one percentage point at large batch sizes; no apparent effect at small batch sizes
rows.note: The intervention helped at large batch sizes but did not establish that it removes the full batch-size penalty.
rows.check: The improvement of up to one percentage point directly demonstrates V5's regularization qualification, which allows shrinking rather than fully eliminating the penalty. The baseline should be the corresponding no-label-smoothing result, not a uniform one-point disadvantage. Budgets are fixed within each batch size but vary between batch sizes, so this is not an equal-epoch comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared steps to reach the goal validation error with different label-smoothing values.

conditions.value: multiple batch sizes
label smoothing; comparisons where multiple values achieved the goal within the training budget

rows.note: The text says label smoothing did not change steps needed when multiple choices achieved the goal within budget.
rows.check: Steps to a fixed validation target measures training speed, not the held-out performance penalty or its removal. The reported absence of a speed change cannot establish absence of V5's effect.
